Section 1

AFRP Strategy

What the Federation's strategy is today, and how each part of it can be carried out in the Hub, building on the member database at its centre.

Where the strategy stands

The Federation has not adopted a plan to follow the Strategic Plan 2018–2023. Its strategy today has four layers, and it is worth being exact about which is which.

  1. The mission. Strengthen the ties between Ramallah people in Palestine and in the United States; give the young people born here their culture and heritage; and educate the American public about Palestinian aspirations.
  2. The commitments still in force. The goals of the 2018–2023 plan, and the 2020–21 Recommendations ("Federation 2.0"). The 2024 by-laws adopted part of the Recommendations outright: the Selection Committee in Article XVII points to them for its details.
  3. The direction set on 10 September 2026. When the Strategic Planning Committee restarted, it asked for a plan built on outcomes and data, an endowment campaign, an Executive Director and a central archive. It named Camp Ramallah, Government Affairs, Arabic classes, Ramallah Works and the Family Tree as current priorities.
  4. The refresh, in draft. The committee's working draft organises the Federation's work on four branches (Education, Leadership, Heritage and Care) and proposes priorities for 2026–27. It is not yet adopted. Until the committee adopts it, the committee's own draft is the text of record (D44); this site shows it and links to it.

Sources. The 2018 SWOT; the Strategic Plan 2018–2023 (May 2019); the 2020–21 Recommendations (3 May 2021) and their working papers; the subcommittee task list; the Convention agreement (October 2022); the committee's minutes from 2020 to 2026; the committee SWOT responses (March 2025); and the committee's 2026 working draft. All of them are listed, with links, on the strategy documents page.

Eight strategic goals

Read side by side, the Federation's documents keep returning to eight goals. The list below is distilled from those documents, for the Strategic Planning Committee to confirm (D52). Each goal has its own page showing what was committed and when, what is still open, how the Hub carries it out and what only people can do.

1. Know and serve every member

This goal is the CRM itself: one record for each person, their household, their clubs, their standing and every payment, in one ledger. Every other goal builds on it.

All branches 8 elements
2. Connect the clubs and the Federation

Clubs work on the same records as the Federation: the club lens, rosters, club groups and follow-ups, club events with check-in, and the remittance ledger that moves dues between them.

All branches 5 elements
3. Bring in and keep the next generation

Each person's place on the branches and on each programme's five rungs sits on their record. The platform can therefore count how many campers became members, instead of guessing.

Education Leadership 11 elements
4. Govern well, and be seen to

The by-laws held as rules, standing computed from the CRM, and elections and digital voting on a frozen electorate. Committee reports and records are proposed next.

All branches 16 elements
5. Speak with one voice

Messages sent from the CRM to the people who consented to receive them, the comms and website desks, the magazine's operations, and the public site.

Heritage Leadership 19 elements
6. Fund the mission, and show the return

Funds and restricted purposes on one ledger across AFRP, ARFECF and ARFHSN, one door for every payment, and outcome reporting for each branch drawn from the same records.

Care 12 elements
7. Keep the heritage and the memory

The family tree is the CRM's spine: every member has a node, and a node is never a lineage claim. The magazine archive and the document registries sit alongside it.

Heritage 4 elements
8. Run the Federation professionally

Roles and access for staff, the Convention element (registration, credentials checked against the remittance ledger, the store, settlement), and events.

The Convention 10 elements

Building on the CRM

Almost every goal depends on one thing being true first: every member is in one database, with their household, their clubs, their standing and their payments. That database is the CRM, and it is the first layer of the Hub. How the Hub builds on the CRM explains the layers and the order they are built in.

The documents

The strategy documents lists every document the strategy is built from, with a summary of each and a link to it in the Federation's shared drive.

Every element, one table

The crosswalk lists every element of the Federation's plans (about eighty-five of them) with what the platform does about each. You can filter it by goal, by status and by section.

What this section does not do

It does not decide anything. Where the Federation's documents are silent or disagree, the pages say so and point to the open questions.

What is real here. By-law citations, decisions and the Federation's own strategy documents are real. People, households and money shown in the prototype and its fixture are fictional. No living person is named on these pages (D50).
